small_guidance:
- The current kernel reorders the loops poorly: it materializes `x_vals` and `w_vals` for every (kd,kh,kw) and then loops over IC inside — swap so IC is the inner GEMM-K axis aggregated across all 27 kernel taps in a single accumulator, or at minimum move the IC loop outside the kd/kh/kw loops to keep `acc` resident. Also try larger BLOCK_N (128/256) since OUT_SPATIAL = 16·30·62·62 ≈ 1.8M is huge per program-N.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32/64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 — the spatial dim dominates and current configs cap BLOCK_N at 128.
- Cache weights: KD·KH·KW·IC·OC = 27·32·64 = 55K floats fits in registers/SMEM if you preload the full weight tile for an OC block once and reuse across all spatial tiles (persistent-OC kernel).
large_guidance:
- Switch to channels-last (NDHWC) layout for both input and output so the IC (and OC) axis is contiguous; this turns the GEMM-K loads into coalesced contiguous reads and lets `tl.dot` consume a `[BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]` × `[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_M]` tile directly without strided gathers per channel.
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM where M = OUT_SPATIAL (per batch), N = OC, K = IC·KD·KH·KW; one program computes a `[BLOCK_M_spatial, BLOCK_N_oc]` output tile by iterating K in BLOCK_K chunks, decoding (ic,kd,kh,kw) from the K index and computing input gather offsets once per K-tile. Fuse bias + mish + tanh in the epilogue (already done). This is the standard high-performance conv layout and removes the triply-nested static_range overhead.
- Consider a persistent kernel that keeps an OC tile of weights resident and streams over (N, spatial) tiles, since weight reuse across the 16·30·62·62 output positions is the dominant arithmetic-intensity lever.
